621	abbrev K3 : K := KT { shared := [3], dealloc := [4], compat := [(4, 104)] } false true
622	
623	/-- One static leaf, `Init` (§47). -/
624	def stZ : Statics := [((none, none, 0), true)]
625	
626	/-- Run R3 (§66, §72, §67, §60, §68, §71, §70, §73): the base frame reads the static 0; frame 1
627	with the provider 1, `x` (2) and the `SharedMutable` leaf 3, 1 and 2 written; 4, `Observe` on 3,
628	writes it by `writeShared`; storage 4 allocated from 1 for `x`, then freed with the authority 104;
629	exit. -/
630	def r3 : List KOp := [.read 0 [0], .enter [] [lf, lf, lf], .write 1 [1] wv, .write 2 [2] wv,
631	  .derive 3 [3] .observe, .writeShared 4 [3] wv, .alloc 1 2 [lf], .free 4 104, .exit]
632	
633	/-- Parameters of R3, fixed once from its final places (§82). -/
634	def π3 : Params Unit := piOf (kernelRun (S3.init stZ) r3).P []
635	
636	/-- State of R3 after its first `n` steps (§82). -/
637	def st3 (n : Nat) : S3 × Machine.State := kfin K3 stZ π3 (r3.take n)
638	
639	/-- **MM23-H05** (material §3, class R). `free` of an allocated root. Expected (material): one
640	`DeallocStep`, compatible authority. Obtained: the same. After seven steps of R3 (reached),
641	`free(4, 104)` is `ok` (§70); it is realized by one raw deallocation of the allocation of 4 with
642	the authority 104, compatible with the recorded token (`FreeCompatInst`, §17.2, §80, §82.4); the
643	`DeallocStep` is `ok` and the allocation is dead afterwards (§17). -/
644	theorem H05 : Sim K3 stZ π3 (st3 7) ∧ Sim K3 stZ π3 (st3 9) ∧
645	    FreeStep K3 4 104 (st3 7).1 (.ok (freeEff (st3 7).1 4)) ∧
646	    opsOf π3 (.free 4 104) (st3 7).1 (st3 7).2 = [.dealloc (π3.L 4).alloc 104] ∧
647	    FreeCompatInst (· = ·) π3.rtok 4 104 ∧
648	    ((st3 7).2.allocs (π3.L 4).alloc).map (·.freeAuth) = some (some 104) ∧
649	    Machine.DeallocStep (· = ·) (π3.L 4).alloc 104 (st3 7).2
650	      (.ok ((st3 7).2.dealloc (π3.L 4).alloc)) ∧
651	    liveOf ((st3 7).2.dealloc (π3.L 4).alloc) (π3.L 4).alloc = some false :=
652	  ⟨sim (by decide) (by decide), sim (by decide) (by decide), .ok (by decide), rfl, by decide,
653	    by decide, .ok (by decide), by decide⟩
654	
655	/-- **MM23-H10** (material §3, class R). Static storage. Expected (material): its allocation is
656	never deallocated. Obtained: the same: every prefix of R3 is a successful translated run and the
657	allocation of the static 0 is live after each of them, the frame exit included (§47: the static is
658	owned by the base frame, which does not exit; §73; §82.6). -/
659	theorem H10 : Sim K3 stZ π3 (st3 9) ∧ ∀ n ∈ List.range (r3.length + 1),
660	    (srun K3 (· = ·) obR obW π3 (sinit stZ π3) (r3.take n)).isSome = true ∧
661	    liveOf (st3 n).2 (π3.L 0).alloc = some true :=
662	  ⟨sim (by decide) (by decide), by decide⟩
663	
664	/-- **MM23-H11** (material §3, class R). Read of an `Init` leaf. Expected (material): `ReadStep`
665	`ok`. Obtained: the same. On the initial state of R3 (reached), the read of the static leaf 0 by
666	the base frame is `ok` (§66); it is realized by one raw read of the range of 0 (§82.2), `ok`
667	(§15), and the range holds the declared initial bytes (§47, §10 ¶5). -/
668	theorem H11 : Sim K3 stZ π3 (st3 0) ∧ Read3Step 0 [0] (st3 0).1 (.ok (st3 0).1) ∧
669	    opsOf π3 (.read 0 [0]) (st3 0).1 (st3 0).2 = [.read (leafAcc (st3 0).2 π3.L .read 0) ()] ∧
670	    Machine.ReadStep obR (leafAcc (st3 0).2 π3.L .read 0) () (st3 0).2
671	      (.ok (readVal (st3 0).2 (leafAcc (st3 0).2 π3.L .read 0))) ∧
672	    (∀ i < 8, bytesOf (st3 0).2 π3.L 0 i = π3.ival 0 i) :=
673	  ⟨sim (by decide) (by decide), .ok (by decide), rfl, readStep_of (by decide), by decide⟩
674	
675	/-- **MM23-H12** (material §3, class R). `writeShared`. Expected (material): an ordinary
676	`WriteStep`, sequential. Obtained: the same. After five steps of R3 (reached), `writeShared` of
677	the `SharedMutable` leaf 3 through the `Observe` authority 4 is `ok` (§68); it is realized by one
678	ordinary raw write of the range of 3 (§82.2), `ok` (§16). Sequential fragment only (§18, §29). -/
679	theorem H12 : Sim K3 stZ π3 (st3 5) ∧ K3.SharedMutable 3 ∧
680	    ((st3 5).1.A[4]?).map (·.mode) = some .observe ∧
681	    WriteSharedStep K3 4 [3] (st3 5).1 (.ok (write3Eff (st3 5).1 [3])) ∧
682	    opsOf π3 (.writeShared 4 [3] wv) (st3 5).1 (st3 5).2 =
683	      [.write (leafAcc (st3 5).2 π3.L .write 3) () (wv 3)] ∧
684	    Machine.WriteStep obW (leafAcc (st3 5).2 π3.L .write 3) () (wv 3) (st3 5).2
685	      (.ok ((st3 5).2.write (leafAcc (st3 5).2 π3.L .write 3) (wv 3))) :=
686	  ⟨sim (by decide) (by decide), by decide, by decide, .ok (by decide), rfl,
687	    .ok ⟨by decide, by decide, trivial⟩⟩
688	
689	/-! ## Run R4: declared disjointness (H01) -/
690	
691	/-- Contract of R4 (§23, §48): `DeclaredDisjoint` is leaf disjointness. -/
692	abbrev K4 : K := KT {} true true
693	
694	/-- Run R4 (§72, §61): frame 1 with the structure 0 of the leaf parts 1 and 2; `split` of its
695	root into the regions `[1]` and `[2]`. -/
696	def r4 : List KOp := [.enter [] [lf, pt 0, pt 0], .split 0 [[1], [2]]]
697	
698	/-- Parameters of R4, fixed once from its final places (§82). -/
699	def π4 : Params Unit := piOf (kernelRun (S3.init []) r4).P []
700	
701	/-- State of R4 after its first `n` steps (§82). -/
702	def st4 (n : Nat) : S3 × Machine.State := kfin K4 [] π4 (r4.take n)
703	
704	/-- **MM23-H01** (material §3, class R). Declared disjointness of two regions sharing a leaf.
705	Expected (material): rejected by `DDSound` (instantiation by leaf disjointness); declared regions
706	have disjoint bytes. Obtained: the same. A contract declaring `[1, 2]` and `[2]` disjoint violates
707	`DDSound` (§80, §23: the normative condition is leaf disjointness); under the contract of R4
708	(`DDSound`, leaf instantiation), after the entry of frame 1 (reached), the `split` of the root
709	into `[1, 2]` and `[2]` is rejected (§61.3). Twin: the `split` into `[1]` and `[2]`, declared
710	disjoint, is `ok` and the run is translated with `Repr`; in its memory state, under `LayoutWF`,
711	every two declared regions of existing leaves have disjoint bytes (§23, §82.1), `[1]` and `[2]`
712	among them. -/
713	theorem H01 : (∀ k : K, k.DeclaredDisjoint [1, 2] [2] → ¬ DDSound k) ∧ DDSound K4 ∧
714	    ¬ K4.DeclaredDisjoint [1, 2] [2] ∧ Sim K4 [] π4 (st4 1) ∧
715	    SplitStep K4 0 [[1, 2], [2]] (st4 1).1 .reject ∧ K4.DeclaredDisjoint [1] [2] ∧
716	    Sim K4 [] π4 (st4 2) ∧
717	    (∀ r r', K4.DeclaredDisjoint r r' → (∀ l ∈ r, l < (st4 2).1.P.length ∧ isLeaf (st4 2).1.P l) →
718	      (∀ l ∈ r', l < (st4 2).1.P.length ∧ isLeaf (st4 2).1.P l) → ByteDisjoint π4.L r r') ∧
719	    ByteDisjoint π4.L [1] [2] := by
720	  have h2 : Sim K4 [] π4 (st4 2) := sim (by decide) (by decide)
721	  have hb : ∀ r r', K4.DeclaredDisjoint r r' →
722	      (∀ l ∈ r, l < (st4 2).1.P.length ∧ isLeaf (st4 2).1.P l) →
723	      (∀ l ∈ r', l < (st4 2).1.P.length ∧ isLeaf (st4 2).1.P l) → ByteDisjoint π4.L r r' :=
724	    fun _ _ hd hr hr' => declaredDisjoint_bytes (KT.ddSound _ _ _) h2.2.2.1.layout hd hr hr'
725	  exact ⟨fun k hd hs => hs _ _ hd 2 (by decide) (by decide), KT.ddSound _ _ _, by decide,
726	    sim (by decide) (by decide), .reject (by decide), by decide, h2, hb,
727	    hb _ _ (by decide) (by decide) (by decide)⟩
728	
729	/-! ## Run R5: references to empty regions (H15) -/
730	
731	/-- Contract of R5 and R6 (§48): nothing declared. -/
732	abbrev K5 : K := KT {} false true
733	
734	/-- Run R5 (§72, §67, §71, §76, §77, §61, §65): frame 1 with the arena value 0, the provider 1,
735	the leaves 2, 3, 4; storage 5 (leaf 6) owned by 0, its root authority 5 the `internal` of the
736	arena; the derived `issue` of the empty region to 2 (block 6: `split` of 5 into `[[]]`, then
737	`store` into 2); `split` of the root of 3 into `[[]]` (authority 7), then `store` of 7 into 4. -/
738	def l5 : List LOp := [.kernel (.enter [] [lf, lf, lf, lf, lf]), .kernel (.write 1 [1] wv),
739	  .kernel (.alloc 1 0 [lf, pt 5]), .kernel (.write 0 [0] wv), .newArena [] 5 5, .issue 0 [] 2,
740	  .kernel (.split 3 [[]]), .kernel (.store 7 4)]
741	
742	/-- Parameters of R5, fixed once from its final places (§82). -/
743	def π5 : Params Unit := piOf (placesOf [] l5) []
744	
745	/-- State of R5 after its first `n` steps (§82.7). -/
746	def lt5 (n : Nat) : LState × Machine.State := lfin K5 [] π5 (l5.take n)
747	
748	/-- **MM23-H15** (material §3, class R). Reference to an empty region, by `issue []` and by
749	`split` into `[]` then `store`. Expected (material): address the base of the allocation of the
750	effective anchor; provenance that allocation. Obtained: the same; the case passes. R5 is reached
751	(`LSim`), the issue being the derived library operation: its raw operations are one write, of the
752	destination 2 (`split` realizes none, §77, §82.7). Block 6 has the empty region, effective anchor
753	5 (the root of the storage), recorded in the arena entry; the range of 2 decodes to the base of
754	the allocation of 5, nonzero, every byte with that allocation as provenance. Authority 7 has the
755	empty region, effective anchor 3; the range of 4 decodes to the base of the allocation of 3,
756	nonzero, with that provenance. Both destinations have the size of a reference (8 bytes). Source of
757	the expected verdict: a decision of the brief recorded for §82.3 (empty-region rule), not stated
758	by spec v0 (§81 leaves encodings to Spec 11). -/
759	theorem H15 : LSim K5 [] π5 (lt5 5) ∧ LSim K5 [] π5 (lt5 8) ∧
760	    (lopsOf π5 (.issue 0 [] 2) (lt5 5).1 (lt5 5).2).map opKind = [1] ∧
761	    (lopsOf π5 (.issue 0 [] 2) (lt5 5).1 (lt5 5).2).map opAlloc = [some (π5.L 2).alloc] ∧
762	    (lt5 8).1.arenas = [⟨5, 5, [6], [([], 6)]⟩] ∧
763	    (lt5 8).1.kern.afp 6 = [] ∧ (lt5 8).1.kern.effAnchor 6 = 5 ∧
764	    anchorAlloc π5.L (lt5 8).1.kern 6 = (π5.L 5).alloc ∧
765	    decodedAt π5 (lt5 8).2 2 = baseOf (lt5 8).2 (π5.L 5).alloc ∧
766	    (∀ i < 8, (bytesOf (lt5 8).2 π5.L 2 i).2 = some (π5.L 5).alloc) ∧
767	    baseOf (lt5 8).2 (π5.L 5).alloc ≠ 0 ∧
768	    (lt5 8).1.kern.afp 7 = [] ∧ (lt5 8).1.kern.effAnchor 7 = 3 ∧
769	    anchorAlloc π5.L (lt5 8).1.kern 7 = (π5.L 3).alloc ∧
770	    decodedAt π5 (lt5 8).2 4 = baseOf (lt5 8).2 (π5.L 3).alloc ∧
771	    (∀ i < 8, (bytesOf (lt5 8).2 π5.L 4 i).2 = some (π5.L 3).alloc) ∧
772	    baseOf (lt5 8).2 (π5.L 3).alloc ≠ 0 ∧ (π5.L 2).len = 8 ∧ (π5.L 4).len = 8 :=
773	  ⟨lsimOf (by decide) (by decide), lsimOf (by decide) (by decide), by decide, by decide,
774	    by decide, by decide, by decide, by decide, by decide, by decide, by decide, by decide,
775	    by decide, by decide, by decide, by decide, by decide, by decide, by decide⟩
776	
777	/-! ## Run R6: a region whose head is not its lowest leaf (H16) -/
778	
779	/-- Run R6 (§72, §67, §71, §76, §77): frame 1 with the arena value 0, the provider 1, the leaf 2;
780	storage 3 (leaves 4 at offset 0 and 5 at offset 8) owned by 0, its root authority 3 the `internal`
781	of the arena; the derived `issue` of the region `[5, 4]` to 2 (block 4). -/
782	def l6 : List LOp := [.kernel (.enter [] [lf, lf, lf]), .kernel (.write 1 [1] wv),
783	  .kernel (.alloc 1 0 [lf, pt 3, pt 3]), .kernel (.write 0 [0] wv), .newArena [] 3 3,
784	  .issue 0 [5, 4] 2]
785	
786	/-- Parameters of R6, fixed once from its final places (§82). -/
787	def π6 : Params Unit := piOf (placesOf [] l6) []
788	
789	/-- State of R6 after its first `n` steps (§82.7). -/
790	def lt6 (n : Nat) : LState × Machine.State := lfin K5 [] π6 (l6.take n)
791	
792	/-- **MM23-H16** (material §3, class R). Reference to a region whose first listed leaf does not
793	have the lowest offset. Expected (material): the lowest address among the nonempty leaves.
794	Obtained: the same; the case passes. R6 is reached (`LSim`), the issue being the derived library
795	operation, realized by one write of the destination 2. Block 4 has the region `[5, 4]`, recorded
796	in the arena entry; both leaves have nonzero size, leaf 4 at offset 0 below the head 5 at offset
797	8; the range of 2 decodes to the address of leaf 4, not to that of the head, every byte with the
798	storage allocation as provenance. Source of the expected verdict: a decision of the brief recorded
799	for §82.3 (lowest-address rule), not stated by spec v0 (§81). -/
800	theorem H16 : LSim K5 [] π6 (lt6 5) ∧ LSim K5 [] π6 (lt6 6) ∧
801	    (lopsOf π6 (.issue 0 [5, 4] 2) (lt6 5).1 (lt6 5).2).map opKind = [1] ∧
802	    (lopsOf π6 (.issue 0 [5, 4] 2) (lt6 5).1 (lt6 5).2).map opAlloc = [some (π6.L 2).alloc] ∧
803	    (lt6 6).1.arenas = [⟨3, 3, [], [([5, 4], 4)]⟩] ∧ (lt6 6).1.kern.afp 4 = [5, 4] ∧
804	    (π6.L 4).off = 0 ∧ (π6.L 5).off = 8 ∧ 0 < (π6.L 4).len ∧ 0 < (π6.L 5).len ∧
805	    leafAddr (lt6 6).2 π6.L 4 < leafAddr (lt6 6).2 π6.L 5 ∧
806	    decodedAt π6 (lt6 6).2 2 = leafAddr (lt6 6).2 π6.L 4 ∧
807	    decodedAt π6 (lt6 6).2 2 ≠ leafAddr (lt6 6).2 π6.L 5 ∧
808	    (∀ i < 8, (bytesOf (lt6 6).2 π6.L 2 i).2 = some (π6.L 3).alloc) ∧ (π6.L 2).len = 8 :=
809	  ⟨lsimOf (by decide) (by decide), lsimOf (by decide) (by decide), by decide, by decide,
810	    by decide, by decide, by decide, by decide, by decide, by decide, by decide, by decide,
811	    by decide, by decide, by decide⟩
812	
813	end Ern.Corpus.MM23H

# ERN — Memory Model Specification v0.1

**Edition v0.1 — corrective candidate, not yet validated**

Modified clauses, relative to v0 (each change is justified by a defect found while formalizing v0):

- §36: `MetaRight` governs authorities over existing storage, not the fresh allocation of `alloc`; §36 and §71.2 contradicted each other.
- §40: `RootHeld` restricted to usable root places, as in §49.7; the two clauses differed on unusable root places.
- §47: the ownership graph of statics is acyclic; a static ownership cycle made §57 false in the initial state.
- §51: a valid origin is an active origin; "valid" was undefined there.
- §57: definition of I5, which v0 named without defining.
- §59: "access operations" are O9–O11; read as all operations, §59 contradicted §69.
- §60.1: a valid origin chain is an active one, read through §44.
- §63.4: the active derived authorities covering the source from outside are named, and the authorities through which the step exercises its `Modify` right are exempt; without this exemption no value could be moved through a derived authority.
- §63.9 (new): the destination is usable in the resulting state; without it an accepted transfer could create an ownership cycle and break §49.8 and §57.
- §69.2 and §70.3: the same exemption as §63.4, and rejection when an authority made inactive by the step keeps an active descendant; without it an accepted step left an active authority with an inactive origin.
- §71.2: the provider is a usable place; v0 did not require it to exist.
- §74 and §75: each `pin` installs an obligation of fresh identity and `unpin` ends one designated obligation; per-leaf pin flags let an `unpin` lift a pin installed by another `pin`.
- §76.6: the reading of the precondition (whole kernel state, `ArenaInv` of the new entry, resulting state); v0 admitted several readings with different verdicts.
- §78.3: restricted to anchors covering a leaf of the administered storage; as written, its second sentence was false.
- §82.2: address and provenance of a pointer to a region whose leaves all have zero physical size; v0 decided no address for that region.
- §86: the last sentence is rewritten; as written, it was false, since `reset` and `issue` leave a recycled leaf `Init` and readable.

**Higher normative authority:** *ERN — Language Charter v0* (October 27, 2026).  
This specification defines the normative rules of ERN's memory model. Technical names (`derive`, `transfer`, `issue`, etc.) designate **abstract semantic operations**; they do not constitute syntax decisions.

## Validation and Revision Procedure

This edition has been validated and acquires normative authority under the ERN Charter v0. Any subsequent semantic change must identify the clauses concerned, justify the change, and preserve the guarantees of the ERN Charter v0. Formal models and proofs are instruments for verifying this specification, not sources of additional rules. Behaviors not determined within its scope are explicitly identified.

## Scope

This specification defines:

- the safe-code contract;
- the abstract machine for allocations, bytes, and accesses;
- the second-class access discipline;
- footprints, authorities, dependencies, frames, and ownership;
- read, write, transfer, release, allocation, and pinning transitions;
- the normative contract of arenas as a reference library abstraction;
- the correspondence obligations between these mechanisms.

It does not define syntax, the complete concurrency model, control-flow conventions, the type system, or compiler lowering. The sequential model's scope does not waive the general guarantees of the Charter.

---

# I. Safe-Behavior Contract

The following contract applies to all safe code and all properly encapsulated abstractions, regardless of their concrete memory representation.

## 1. Definitions of Safe Behavior

**Safe operation:** An operation that imposes no unchecked safety obligation on its user whose violation could compromise the language's guarantees.

**Safe code:** Code that executes only safe operations and does not directly assume obligations specific to unsafe operations.

**Safe interface:** An interface whose every permitted use preserves the language's guarantees when its implementation is correct.

**Safe abstraction:** An abstraction exposing a safe interface; its implementation may use unsafe operations provided it fulfills all their obligations.

## 46. Arenas as Library Administration States

Each entry belongs to the library's abstract state, **separate from kernel state `S₃`**. It has the following fields:

```text
ArenaEntry {
    storage: PlaceId
    internal: AuthorityId
    available: Set<Leaf>
    issued: Set<(Region, AuthorityId)>
}
```

A region is **available if and only if each of its leaves belongs to `available`**; the empty region is always available. Issuance removes the leaves of the issued region from `available`. Reset restores all leaves of the administered storage to that set. The registry and its updates belong to the abstraction contract and create no kernel permissions.

The arena is **live** if `internal` is active. The **arena value** is the place holding `internal`, distinct from the possible owner of `storage`. Administered storage may be local, static, allocated, or issued by another arena, under `newArena` preconditions and applicable invariants. `available` and `issued` remain **in the library's arena entry**.

## 47. Initial State

The kernel's initial state contains only base frame 0 and the declared static storage. Every static leaf has its declared initial state, `Init` or `Uninit`. The roots of static places directly owned by frame 0 have a root `Modify` authority held by that frame; a static may also be owned by another static, in which case its root authority is held by the latter. The ownership graph of statics is acyclic: no static is owned, directly or transitively, by itself. The initial state invents no dynamic allocation, derived authority, or implicit anchor. The initial arena registry belongs to library state and is empty. The initial frame does not exit.

## 48. External Parametric Contract

`K` contains the predicates `DeclaredDisjoint`, `SharedMutable`, `Pinned`, `ExternalDone`, `Deallocable`, `FreeCompat`, and `Satisfiable`. Their obligations are specified in Section 80. `K` can neither fabricate access rights nor remove an obligation of the Charter. The predicate `Invalidates` is not part of this contract.

# VII. Invariants of Reachable States

Machine states are subject to structural, validity, and exclusivity requirements preserved by permitted transitions under their declared external contracts.

## 49. WF3 — Well-Formedness of Frames, Places, and Authorities

`WF3(s)` is a **predicate on state `s`**. It jointly requires:

1. a nonempty, duplicate-free frame stack, every frame having a valid identity and, except for the base frame, a valid parent; frame-parent relations are well-founded;
2. a place structure whose composition links are valid and **acyclic**; every structural part shares its parent's owner and death marker;
3. valid owners of type frame or place, and **well-founded** ownership chains reaching a live frame for every usable place;
4. footprints consisting exclusively of leaves of existing places;
5. authorities with valid identities and modes, whose existing origins form **acyclic** chains ending at a root authority;
6. `RootChain`: every origin chain of an authority covering a leaf ends at the root of the **same structural root place** as that leaf;
7. `RootHeld`: every usable root place has its active root `Modify` authority, with no origin, held exactly by its owner;
8. holder validity: every active authority is held by a frame present in the stack or by a usable place.

Numerical ordering of identifiers, parent precedence over child in a list, and bounds on generated identifiers may be used **to represent or prove** this well-formedness in a formalization; they are not normative restrictions on place or authority identities. Preservation of `WF3` by a transition is a **required property of transitions**, not an additional clause of the state predicate. `WF3` does not impose any particular physical object layout: that belongs to refinement into the elementary memory machine.

## 50. I1 — Structural Exclusivity

For two active authorities **unrelated by derivation** covering the same leaf, their own modes must both be `Observe`. This rule also applies to leaves identified as `SharedMutable`; their particular mutation is governed by the `writeShared` contract and creates no exception to I1.

Exclusivity of **effective** modes (`effective_exclusive`) is a consequence of I1 and the definition of `effective`, not the definition of I1. On a leaf, two incompatible authorities cannot simultaneously possess incompatible effective rights. The only permitted independent ordinary coexistence is `Observe` / `Observe`.

## 51. I2 — Conservation of Rights

A derived authority covers only a subfootprint of what its origin chain permits and does not elevate its mode. Derivation and splitting restrictions do not allow duplication of an exclusive right over a leaf. Every active authority is linked to a valid origin according to state and reanchoring rules: an origin is **valid** if and only if it is active, so the origin of an active derived authority is active. Partial suspension follows from `effective`.

## 52. I3 — Validity of Anchors and Dependencies

Every explicit anchor of a still-usable place is valid. An operation cannot invalidate an anchor retained by a place that remains usable. Transitive propagation of dependencies from contained values does not change this obligation. Dependencies are not permissions and are insufficient to justify an access.

## 53. I4 — Consumption and Movement

A `Moved` leaf cannot be read as if it still contained its previous value. Moving a value does not preserve two copies of an exclusive authority. Initialization state and authority-exercise state are separate checks.

## 54. Anchor Ordering and Absence of Orphan Rights

`AnchorOrder` and `AnchorOrderHeld` are defined in Section 44. `NoDangling` prohibits an **active** authority from covering a leaf belonging to an unusable place; the invariant does not say that a leaf is initialized. `NoOrphan` requires every active authority held by a place to be connected to a frame in the stack through a **finite, non-repeating chain** of authorities: the first link is held by a live frame, and each active link **structurally covers the entirety** of the place holding the next link. The link need not have an effective mode over that place. `NoOrphan` guarantees neither the exercisability of all stored authorities nor freedom from blocking.

## 55. ArenaInv — Invariant of the Arena Abstraction

`ArenaInv` is an invariant of the **library contract**, not an additional predicate of kernel state. For every live arena:

- `storage` designates an existing, usable place; the footprint of `internal` is exactly the footprint of `storage`;
- `internal` is active, with own mode `Modify`, held by the arena value;
- available leaves and issued regions belong to the administered storage;
- two still-active issuances have disjoint regions; no leaf of a still-issued region simultaneously belongs to `available`;
- every still-issued block authority is a derivative of `internal` complying with exclusivity and validity rules;
- anchor and ownership restrictions are respected.

Arena entries do not, by themselves, constitute an additional storage owner. Two live arenas may cover common leaves when their `internal` authorities are distinct and their effective rights are compatible; no **global** disjointness of arena footprints is imposed.

## 56. Uniqueness of Live Administration

**An authority identity may serve as `internal` for at most one live administrative abstraction**, whether an arena, `HandlePool`, `DataStack`, or another library administrative instance. Before registering a new abstraction, its creation operation must jointly check the absence of that identity from **all relevant registries of live administrations**. Uniqueness concerns the identity of the `internal` authority, not merely possible overlap of footprints: abstractions with distinct `internal` identities are not forbidden merely because their footprints overlap. Library contracts must make the information required for this guard available to the creation operation; checking only an abstraction's own registry is insufficient.

**This guard is not a condition for any safety property in Section 57.** The effective right (Section 43, case 3) already prohibits a second issuance over leaves covered by an active block derived from the same authority. Rather, the guard preserves the **abstraction contract**: without it, simultaneous administration of the same `internal` could cause `reject` instead of `fail`, or reissue a previously released block that the first administration still considers unavailable. It creates neither permissions nor allocations and introduces no general detection of authority cycles. Its physical representation and encapsulation of library registries remain outside the kernel.

## 57. Main Invariant

\[
Inv3 = I1 \land I2 \land I3 \land I4 \land AnchorOrder \land NoDangling
\]

On states reachable from `S3.init statics` under `DDSound(K)`, the kernel guarantees:

\[
WF3 \land Inv3 \land AnchorOrderHeld \land NoOrphan
\]

`ArenaInv` (Section 55) belongs to the library abstraction: it is not included in this main kernel invariant.

**I5:** every pinned leaf, statically (`K.Pinned`) or dynamically (an active pinning obligation, Section 74), belongs to a usable place.

I5, associated with pinned storage, remains a **specialized obligation** of `K.Pinned`, not a clause automatically implied by sequential accesses alone. This property is required for reachable states under the declared assumptions. Its correspondence with allocations and bytes requires the refinement defined below.

# VIII. Definition of Transitions and Management of Authorities

The following operations are abstract transition rules. They distinguish rejection by the discipline, defined failure, and a permitted transition.

## 58. Transition Outcomes

Every operation has a conceptual outcome among:

```text
Outcome3 = ok(new_state) | reject | fail
```

`reject` means that the static discipline does not permit the step; it is neither an implicit runtime trap nor `ub` in the elementary memory machine. `fail` is a **defined failure** leaving the state unchanged; **only `alloc` may produce it in the O1–O16 kernel**. Other kernel operations produce `ok` or `reject`. Library-abstraction operations, including `issue` (§77), may define their own `fail` cases. Where such failure is provided, static preconditions are checked before dynamic availability, according to the operation's contract.

An `ok` transition must satisfy its preconditions, apply exactly its prescribed effects, and preserve the relevant invariants. No transition fabricates a permission to make its conclusion true. Holder and anchor changes are evaluated in the **resulting state** when a rule explicitly so provides.

## 59. Implicit Preservation of Modes and Anchors

Changes in effective authority are **derived** from active authorities and their origins; no `Suspended` indicator is mutated. Access operations (O9–O11) do not change an anchor without an explicitly authorized effect of transfer, `depend`, `store`, release, or reanchoring. Leaves becoming `Init` do so through a permitted write (`write3`, `writeShared`, `store`, including during a derived `issue`) or a transfer from a corresponding source leaf already `Init`; leaves initialized in `S3.init` are declared as such.

## 60. O1 — Derivation of an Authority

**Preconditions**

1. `source` is an active derived or root authority, and `ExercisableAt(s,source,mode)` holds; its origin chain and anchors are valid: every authority of its origin chain, its effective anchor included, is active.
2. The leaves of `region` exist and belong to the footprint of `source`; `mode` does not exceed the available effective right on these leaves.
3. The addition preserves exclusivity I1: no unrelated active authority becomes incompatible with the derived right, and already-active descendants are respected.
4. The new holding frame is the live current frame. The admissible state's footprint and anchoring restrictions remain true.

**`ok` effect:** A new active authority with fresh identity, origin `source`, requested mode and footprint, and held by the current frame is added. The source remains active; its effective modes are recomputed per leaf. No storage or place anchor is created. Multiple compatible observations remain permitted. **Other outcome:** `reject`.

## 61. O2 — Splitting Authorities

**Preconditions**

1. `source` is active and exercisable by the current frame with sufficient modification rights over the relevant leaves.
2. Each region lies within the available, effectively modifiable footprint of the source.
3. Regions are pairwise disjoint under structural composition or contract `K.DeclaredDisjoint`, subject to obligation `DDSound(K)`; no exclusive right already distributed is overlapped.
4. Creation of the derivatives respects origins, conservation I1/I2, and validity obligations.

**`ok` effect:** An active derived `Modify` authority held by the current frame is created for each region. `source` remains active; its effective modification capability disappears only over distributed leaves and remains on undistributed leaves. Authorities are split logically: `split` performs no physical allocation. **Other outcome:** `reject`.

An unjustified declaration of disjointness may invalidate the proof: without `DDSound`, an accepted `split` may violate I1. Constructing zero-sized subregions is not identified with an allocation of the elementary memory machine; the case of an empty shape in `alloc` is distinct.

## 62. O3 — End of a Derived Borrow

**Preconditions**

1. `authority` is active **and derived**: an authority with no origin is rejected.
2. It is held by the current frame, or by a place `p` on which the current frame has exercisable `Modify`.
3. No active descendant of the authority prevents its release; no other still-usable value may lose a required anchor.
4. If the authority is stored in its holding place, that place is exempted from the check “this authority still appears among the anchors” **only because the effect removes that anchor at the same time**. An anchor with the same identity attached by `depend` to another usable place continues to block the step.
5. Applicable abstraction contracts remain satisfied.

**`ok` effect:** The authority becomes inactive and can no longer be exercised. It is removed from its holding place's anchors when stored there. Effective modes of its origins are recomputed, allowing unblocked rights to return. There is no implicit deallocation. **Other outcome:** `reject`.

# IX. Transfer, Dependencies, and Storage of Rights

These transitions govern value consumption and the controlled movement of their dependencies. A valid transition can neither create an additional permission nor discard a surviving anchor.

## 63. O4 — Consuming Value Transfer

**Preconditions**

1. `source` and `destination` are usable, and the current frame has exercisable `Modify` over their relevant footprints.
2. Source and destination have the **same shape of ordered subtrees**. The `i`-th child of each source part corresponds to the `i`-th child of the corresponding destination part; all nodes are matched. Structural field identity is positional, not an arbitrary matching of children.
3. **All** source leaves are `Init`, and **no** destination leaf is `Init`. The source and destination footprints are disjoint.
4. No exclusive authority is duplicated; validity of derived authorities and active projections is preserved. No active derived authority held outside `source` covers a source leaf, except the authorities through which the step exercises its `Modify` right over `source`: the exercisable authority on which that right rests and its origin chain. Other active authorities remain subject to this check.
5. **No in-place source leaf is pinned**, either statically (`K.Pinned`) or dynamically (`pin`). Storage merely **owned** by the source, which is not itself moved by the transfer of that value, does not prevent this transfer.
6. Dependencies of all still-usable places following the value remain valid; non-escape constraints and `AnchorOrder` are checked in the **resulting state**, including transferred anchors of owned places that remain usable.
7. All moved held authorities, including those of owned storage, satisfy `AnchorOrderHeld` in the resulting state; no authority may escape a local anchor on the grounds that its containing value was transferred.
8. **Local self-blocking prevention:** For each active authority held before the step by a part `r` of `source` whose holder becomes the corresponding part `corr(r)` of `destination`, that authority's footprint contains **no leaf** of `corr(r)` in the resulting state. Transfer is rejected if this local check fails; no global authority-acyclicity check is imposed.
9. **Destination usability:** `destination` is usable in the resulting state.

**`ok` effect:**

- every source leaf becomes `Moved` and each corresponding destination leaf becomes `Init`;
- every authority held by source part `r` acquires as its new holder the corresponding destination part `corr(r)`, not indiscriminately the destination root;
- places owned by `r` become owned by `corr(r)`; their roots follow this owner according to `RootHeld`;
- value dependencies follow the corresponding places under validity guarantees; no authority is created or duplicated;
- destination places receive the transferred values and rights without automatically moving storage not owned by a source part.

**Other outcome:** `reject`. `transfer` to a call result is subject to these same rules.

A partially initialized structure may be transferred **field by field**, but only for fields individually eligible for transfer. This does not automatically destructure a value that owns storage **at the container level**: that storage stays with the container if the container is not transferred. Conversion between structures with permuted fields must be handled separately, not as a `transfer`.

## 64. O5 — Explicit Attachment of an Anchor

**Preconditions**

1. `result` is a usable place over which the current frame has exercisable `Modify`.
2. `anchor` designates an active, valid authority representing a real dependency of the relevant rights or storage; a declared dependency cannot extend an origin's lifetime.
3. Existing anchors are preserved and the addition respects `AnchorOrder`: the effective anchor's frame is the frame of `result` or an ancestor thereof.
4. Every dependency carried by a contained value remains represented in the transitive obligations of its container.

15	5. **In the resulting state**, `target` remains under exercisable `Modify` by the current frame (`store_keeps_target_reachable`), and `AnchorOrderHeld` remains true. This is a genuine additional precondition, not an automatic consequence of the preceding ones.
16	
17	**`ok` effect:** The holder of `authority` becomes `target`; the authority is added to `D(target)`; **only** leaf `target` becomes `Init`. Other fields of a structure, even adjacent ones, do not change their initialization state. **Other outcome:** `reject`.
18	
19	Overwriting an active authority already held by the leaf is prohibited; its explicit release may make the target reusable. The resulting-state clause does not by itself prohibit all cycles possible after other operations: general freedom from blocking (`NoLock`) is not adopted here.
20	
21	# X. Reading, Writing, and Initialization
22	
23	A leaf's initialization state and the effective right to access it are two distinct conditions.
24	
25	## 66. O9 — Safe Reading of Regions
26	
27	**Preconditions**
28	
29	1. Every leaf being read belongs to a usable place and is `Init`.
30	2. `access` is an authority exercisable in `Observe` mode over the region; its **effective** mode actually permits observation of each leaf being read.
31	3. Required anchors are valid, and the type and storage contract permits this read.
32	
33	**`ok` effect:** The logical read succeeds, without modifying `F`, `P`, `I`, `A`, `D`, or arena entries. **Other outcome:** `reject`.
34	
35	`Moved` and `Uninit` cannot be read. This definition does not replace concrete representation and pointer checks of the elementary memory machine.
36	
37	## 67. O10 — Ordinary Write
38	
39	**Preconditions**
40	
41	1. Targeted leaves belong to usable places, and `access` is exercisable in `Modify` mode with **effective** `Modify` right over each leaf.
42	2. No incompatible ordinary authority holds an incompatible effective mode over the written leaves (I1).
43	3. Anchors and constraints of the relevant types, storage, and abstractions remain valid.
44	
45	**`ok` effect:** The logical write sets the actually written leaves to `Init` and does not modify authorities or their anchors. An unwritten leaf does not become `Init` by this effect. **Other outcome:** `reject`.
46	
47	## 68. O11 — Write Under Shared Mutation
48	
49	**Preconditions**
50	
51	1. Every leaf in the region is usable and declared `K.SharedMutable`.
52	2. `access` is exercisable in a mode **at least** `Observe` and has a present effective mode on every leaf, either `Observe` or `Modify`; exercising an authority without an effective mode is insufficient.
53	3. Dependencies are valid and the particular shared-mutation discipline guaranteed by `K.SharedMutable` applies.
54	
55	**`ok` effect:** Actually written leaves become `Init`; authorities and their structural exclusivity I1 do not change. **Other outcome:** `reject`.
56	
57	`writeShared` may update metadata under an `Observe` authority when the contract permits. Stability of observed contents is not automatically guaranteed, and this kernel **does not prove** the absence of data races: that requires the concurrency model's guarantees.
58	
59	# XI. End of Use, Deallocation, and Allocation
60	
61	The logical end of a value does not necessarily entail deallocation of its storage. The following operations treat initialization, ownership, and physical release separately.
62	
63	## 69. O12 — Logical End of a Value's Use
64	
65	**Preconditions**
66	
67	1. `place` is usable and the current frame has exercisable `Modify` over it.
68	2. No active descendant over the leaves of `place` **or storage that dies with it** is held outside the places dying with `place`, in a way that would prevent rights from returning or being invalidated. The authorities through which the step exercises its `Modify` right over `place`, namely the exercisable authority on which that right rests and its origin chain, are exempt from this check. Moreover, no authority that the effect makes inactive (held by `place` or by a place dying with it, transitively owned storage included) has an active descendant, whatever its footprint, that the same step does not make inactive.
69	3. No place **remaining usable after the effect** depends on an authority held by `place`, its root, or an authority that would become inactive when an owned holder dies.
70	4. **No leaf whose use ends, including transitively owned storage, is pinned**, either statically (`K.Pinned`) or dynamically (`pin`). A dynamic pinning obligation must be legally removed by `unpin` before this step.
71	
72	**`ok` effect:** The leaves of value `place` become `Uninit`; `place` **remains usable as a place** and may legally be reinitialized. Authorities held by `place` and dead substorages are released; dependencies of the ended value are removed; transitively owned places that cease to live are marked dead. The operation does not automatically trigger physical deallocation in the elementary memory machine: an unfreed allocation may constitute a leak, which this guarantee does not prohibit. **Other outcome:** `reject`.
73	
74	## 70. O13 — Release of an Owned Storage Unit
75	
76	**Preconditions**
77	
78	1. `place` is a **root of storage owned by a value** (`OwnedRoot`), not an ordinary local directly owned by a frame and not part of an aggregate.
79	2. `K.Deallocable(place)` is established, and `K.FreeCompat(place,auth)` justifies deallocation authority `auth`; this identifier is opaque to the authority kernel.
80	3. The current frame has exercisable `Modify`; no active derivative over the footprint being freed is held outside holders that die; no surviving place is anchored to an authority of the released region or of its dead holders. The authorities through which the step exercises its `Modify` right over `place`, namely the exercisable authority on which that right rests and its origin chain, are exempt from the check on active derivatives. Moreover, no authority that the effect makes inactive (an authority of the released region, its root included, or an authority whose holder dies) has an active descendant, whatever its footprint, that the same step does not make inactive.
81	4. No leaf of the released unit is statically or dynamically pinned. Ending external use does not silently turn a still-pinned leaf into a releasable unit.
82	
83	**`ok` effect:** `place` and the storage that ceases to live are marked dead; authorities of those regions, including their corresponding roots, become inactive, as do authorities whose holders die. Surviving dependencies must remain valid. Every realization of `free` must satisfy the corresponding deallocation relation of the elementary memory machine (Part III). **Other outcome:** `reject`.
84	
85	## 71. O14 — Allocation of a New Storage Root
86	
87	**Static preconditions**
88	
89	1. `shape` is a **nonempty** abstract shape, represented like the local places of `enterFrame`; an allocation of **zero physical size** may be represented by a logical one-leaf shape.
90	2. The provider is a usable place, and **all leaves of the provider** are `Init`; updates to its metadata are permitted through exercisable `Modify` or a valid `writeShared` over `SharedMutable` metadata.
91	3. The current frame has exercisable `Modify` over `owner`; new identities and ownership relations must respect `WF3`, `RootHeld`, and liveness restrictions.
92	
93	**Outcomes**
94	
95	- `reject`: a static precondition does not hold;
96	- `fail`: static preconditions hold, but `K.Satisfiable(provider,shape,s)` is false in the state under consideration; **no state change**;
97	- `ok(s')`: creation of a **new storage root** with fresh identity, owned by `owner`; its leaves start `Uninit`, its new root `Modify` authority with no origin is held by `owner`; provider metadata is updated only in accordance with its modification rights.
98	
99	Allocation success depends on the provider's state: it does not constitute a right to invent physical memory. Any realization of this operation must satisfy the `AllocStep` relation defined by the rules of Sections 9 and 13.
100	
101	# XII. Call Frames and Return of Authorities
102	
103	Frames are execution units that receive authorities, introduce locals, and have exit rules distinct from Spec 3's value-passing conventions.
104	
105	## 72. O6 — Entering a Frame
106	
107	**Preconditions**
108	
109	1. The calling frame is the current frame and is live. Each parameter passed to the callee is an active, derived authority held by the caller before the step; the caller is **not necessarily** the frame in which the authority was first derived.
110	2. Modes, footprints, anchoring, and parameter-passing rules permit this change of holder; introduction of locals preserves well-formedness and the validity of their roots.
111	3. **Origin protection on entry:** for each `Modify` parameter with direct origin `o`, `o` is exercisable in **no mode** (neither `Observe` nor `Modify`) in the **resulting state**, once the new frame's parameters and locals have been created.
112	4. **G4:** `AnchorOrderHeld` is checked over the complete resulting state.
113	
114	**`ok` effect:** A new child frame is pushed onto the stack; active parameters **are yielded** to that frame, which becomes their sole holder; local places and their root authorities are created; valid anchors inherited from the caller are preserved. This transfer creates no additional rights. **Other outcome:** `reject`.
115	
116	This clause establishes **entry protection**. It does not prove the stronger property of protection throughout the **entire** invocation following other releases or reanchorings. While a `Modify` parameter remains active, its direct origin remains subject to effective-mode restrictions. Any additional protection throughout the invocation is deferred to Spec 3.
117	
118	## 73. O7 — Exiting a Frame
119	
120	**Preconditions**
121	
122	1. The current frame is not the initial frame and has a surviving caller.
123	2. Results that must survive have already been legally transferred to their destinations; no active authority or dependency may remain invalidly attached to locals that are about to die.
124	3. **No leaf of a place that dies with the frame, including transitively owned storage, is pinned**, either statically (`K.Pinned`) or dynamically (`pin`).
125	4. Iterated reanchoring of surviving authorities and anchors reaches the **first surviving active origin**, held either by a surviving frame or by a usable place whose terminal owner survives; it is not permitted to skip a surviving origin merely because it is held by a place. The operation is rejected when no suitable surviving origin exists, particularly if the chain reaches a root of the exiting frame.
126	5. Validity of anchors of surviving values and `AnchorOrderHeld` are checked **in the resulting state**. Other state invariants and resource contracts are respected.
127	
128	**`ok` effect:**
129	
130	- the current frame is removed from the stack; its untransferred locals and substorages dying with them become unusable;
131	- authorities still held by that frame, or by places that have become unusable, are released;
132	- origins of surviving derived authorities are reanchored to the **first surviving active origin** of their chains, whether held by a frame or a usable place, and the `D` anchors of surviving values are correspondingly reanchored;
133	- reanchoring changes **neither the footprint nor the own mode** of an authority; parameter identities and relations specific to the frame cease their operational role;
134	- the calling frame becomes current again.
135	
136	**Other outcome:** `reject`. Exiting does not entail automatic physical deallocation of all dead places. Deferred cleanup (`defer`) lies outside this kernel. Reanchoring may change the current `origin` relation; protection of a historical borrow lineage during an invocation is a distinct, deferred question.
137	
138	# XIII. Pinning, Statics, and External Commitments
139	
140	Pinning forbids certain movements or ends of lifetime. It is not a general guarantee of content immutability.
141	
142	## 74. O15 — Dynamic Pinning
143	
144	**Preconditions:** `place` is usable, the current frame has exercisable `Modify` over the relevant leaves, and the operation respects applicable pinning obligations.
145	
146	**`ok` effect:** A dynamic pinning obligation of fresh identity is installed on the relevant leaves. A leaf is dynamically pinned while at least one active pinning obligation covers it. While an obligation is active, `transfer`, `endUse`, `free`, and `exitFrame` are rejected if they act on leaves it pins; removal of this obligation requires `unpin` under `K.ExternalDone`. Pinning does not make contents immutable. **Other outcome:** `reject`.
147	
148	## 75. O16 — Removal of Dynamic Pinning
149	
150	**Preconditions:** `unpin` designates one active dynamic pinning obligation, installed by `pin` on `place`; `place` is usable, the current frame has exercisable `Modify`, and contract `K.ExternalDone`, applied to that obligation, attests that all relevant external use has ended.
151	
152	**`ok` effect:** The designated dynamic pinning obligation ends, and only that one: a leaf it covered stays pinned while another active obligation covers it. The step does not itself modify values, their initialization, or their access authorities. Static obligations are not removed by this operation. **Other outcome:** `reject`.
153	
154	**Associated static rule (`StaticPinnedBottom`):** Statics designated by `K.Pinned` must be places **directly** owned by the **base frame**, not merely transitively owned by a static value. This restriction ensures that they do not die when an intermediate frame exits.
155	
156	# XIV. Arenas and Collective Invalidation — Reference Abstraction
157	
158	An arena is a **library abstraction**, not a memory-kernel primitive. Operations O17 through O19 are **derived** from operations O1 through O16 and abstraction-specific metadata: `newArena` registers an administration without modifying the kernel; `issue` performs `split` followed by `store` (after checking availability); `reset` performs a `Modify` derivation over all storage—through `derive` or `split`—then `release`, before restoring availability. Their contract below is **normative for the standard-library arena** until Spec 10 takes responsibility for it. It authorizes neither new permissions nor an additional access machine. Arena entries (Section 46) constitute the abstract state of this administration; the guard in Section 56 belongs to its consistency contract. The contracts of `HandlePool` and `DataStack` belong to their library abstractions and are not defined here.
159	
160	## 76. O17 — Creation of an Administered Arena
161	
162	**Preconditions**
163	
164	1. `storage` is an existing, usable place under exercisable `Modify` by the current frame. It may be local, static, allocated, or a block issued by a previous arena.
165	2. `internal` is explicitly named by the caller, exists, is active, has own mode `Modify`, and `ExercisableAt(s,internal,Modify)` holds.
166	3. `internal` is **held by a place**: that place is the arena value; `footprint(internal) = footprint(storage)`.
167	4. **Unified administration guard (Section 56):** no **live** administrative abstraction, whether an arena or a library instance such as a handle pool, already uses this `internal` identity. The relevant registries of library administrations are consulted before registration. Two distinct identities may cover common leaves: this is not in itself grounds for rejection.
168	5. All leaves of the arena value holding `internal` are already `Init`; construction does not initialize them implicitly.
169	6. Dependency, holder, storage, and administration relations respect, in the resulting state, `WF3`, I1, `AnchorOrder`, and `AnchorOrderHeld` over the whole kernel state, and the new entry satisfies `ArenaInv` (Section 55).
170	
171	**`ok` effect:** A live entry `{storage, internal, available, issued}` is added; the initial `available` set represents the administered storage, and `issued` is initially empty. Registering the entry fabricates no place, access right, or `Init` state. **Other outcome:** `reject`.
172	
173	The identity of `internal`, not the index of `storage`, is the key to preventing duplication of live administrations. No global constraint requires footprints of live arenas to be pairwise disjoint.
174	
175	## 77. O18 — Issuing an Arena Block
176	
177	**Static preconditions**
178	
179	1. The `arena` entry exists and is live; `internal` is active. `MetaRight` requires exercisable `Modify` over the arena value holding `internal` (Section 36). Mutation of metadata through `writeShared` alone does not satisfy this condition.
180	2. `region` belongs to the administered storage; `destination` is a usable **leaf** holding no active authority; the destination can legally receive the block value in mode `Modify`. The fact that `destination` is already `Init` is not in itself grounds for rejection, in accordance with O8.2.
181	   **Local self-blocking prevention: leaf `destination` is not in `region`, including when the region is declared available.** This condition is static and is checked before an availability `fail`.
182	3. Applicable **static** validity and non-escape restrictions for the destination are satisfied. The `AnchorOrder` check depending on the new anchor is performed on the **simulated resulting state**, after the availability check described in point 4; it cannot turn an unavailable issuance (`fail`) into `reject`.
183	
184	**Availability and exercisability checks**
185	
186	4. If static conditions hold but **at least one leaf of `region` does not belong to `available`**, the operation produces **`fail` and leaves the entire state unchanged**. The empty region is always available. An unavailable region does not permit a prior static rejection to be bypassed.
187	5. If the region is available, the effective mode of `internal` on that region must permit `Modify`; otherwise the outcome is `reject`.
188	6. The simulated result must satisfy `AnchorOrderHeld` **in the resulting state**; moreover, **in that resulting state, `destination` must remain under exercisable `Modify` by the current frame**, in accordance with O8.5. Issuance into a value with a longer lifetime than a local anchor is not made valid merely by storing it in the caller.
189	
190	**`ok` effect:** A block authority of fresh identity, derived from `internal` and of mode `Modify`, is issued for the region; it is held by `destination`, which receives the corresponding anchor. The leaves of the region leave `available`, and the issuance is added to `issued` with its authority. **Only leaf `destination` becomes `Init`**; no other leaf of the arena value changes initialization. Previous issuances remain intact and valid. Issuance does not automatically install anchors on third-party values: they must use their lawful dependency mechanisms.
191	
192	**Outcomes:** `ok`, `fail` (region unavailable after static validation), `reject` (static rule, effective right, or anchoring not satisfied). The destination may be a leaf of the arena value itself: its initialization then constitutes **an explicit write to that destination**, not implicit initialization of the entire arena value's metadata.
193	
194	## 78. O19 — Collective Arena Reset
195	
196	**Preconditions**
197	
198	1. The entry exists and is live. **`MetaRight(s,arena)` requires exercisable `Modify` over the arena value**, in accordance with Section 36. `writeShared` over metadata alone, even when legal, does not replace such exercise. `internal` and the arena's other restrictions remain valid.
199	2. **No active authority derived from `internal` covers a leaf of the administered storage.** A derived authority with an empty footprint does not, by itself, block `reset`.
200	3. No still-usable place depends, directly or transitively, on an anchor in the **strict origin subtree of `internal`** (`internal` itself is excluded) that covers a leaf of the administered storage. Under precondition 2 and invariant I3, this condition follows from the absence of active descendants covering the storage, and remains explicit in the abstraction contract. Validity obligations of other nested arenas remain satisfied.
201	
202	**`ok` effect:** All **leaves** of the administered storage become available again, and the issuance list is cleared under the arena contract. No still-active derived authority covering those leaves may remain, by precondition 2; an empty-footprint derivative may remain active without designating any recycled leaf. **No leaf is made `Init` by `reset`**, including in the arena value. **Other outcome:** `reject`.
203	
204	Safe reuse after `reset` requires that previous issuances **covering recycled leaves**, and the dependencies on which their validity rests, have effectively ceased preventing their reuse. Any active empty-footprint derivatives cover none of those leaves. A historically issued region does not remain permanently unavailable solely for that reason.
205	
206	# XV. Transitive Dependencies, Returns, and Value Behavior
207	
208	Dependent values may survive transfers and calls only if the required anchors and rights remain valid. Second-class access does not imply an arbitrary persistent reference.
209	
210	## 79. Non-Escaping Values and Returns
211	
212	The second-class nature of access authorities does not prohibit constructing a value carrying a derived authority or returning a result dependent on a caller-owned resource. What is prohibited is artificially extending the validity of a local origin.
213	
214	A typical scenario is:
215	
216	```text
217	arena = create_arena()
218	buffer = create_buffer(arena)
219	use(buffer)
220	endUse(buffer)       // or equivalent release of its dependent rights
221	arena.reset()
222	```
223	
224	The scenario is permitted when:
225	
226	1. the call receives and exercises valid authorities over the arena;
227	2. issuance supplies a block disjoint from live issuances;
228	3. the result value is anchored to the rights actually required;
229	4. its transfer to the caller respects `SameShape`, holders, `AnchorOrder`, and `AnchorOrderHeld`;
230	5. `exitFrame` can reanchor surviving authorities without using a dead local root;
231	6. `reset` is rejected while the dependent result or a block authority remains active, then becomes permitted after those rights have effectively ended.
232	
233	A “non-escaping” value is therefore not necessarily confined to the frame in which it was created. It may survive a function when it depends on a caller anchor, without extending dead local storage. This result does **not** imply strong protection of all parameter authorities throughout the entire invocation: the historical interpretation of reborrows and this property are deferred to Spec 3.
234	
235	Properties of transfer between threads and shareability do not follow from this sequential model alone. They depend on external resources, contained authorities, anchors, confinement restrictions, and the concurrency model of Spec 2.
236	
237	# XVI. External Contracts and Interfaces with Other Specifications
238	
239	Declarative contracts create no rights. Their satisfaction is an obligation of the language, typing, implementation, or a safe abstraction, according to the nature of each contract.
240	
241	## 80. Parametric Contracts of the Access Discipline
242	
243	A contract `K` parameterizes rules of the access discipline without fabricating permissions. A safe abstraction using part of `K` must prove or fulfill the corresponding obligation; an unestablished precondition is not a language guarantee.
244	
245	| Contract | External obligation |
246	|---|---|
247	| `DeclaredDisjoint` | `DDSound(K)`: no falsely declared disjoint region when leaves can overlap |
248	| `Pinned` | I5, prohibition of incompatible physical moves; `StaticPinnedBottom` for pinned statics |
249	| `SharedMutable` | Applicable shared-mutation discipline, with correct rights and synchronization |
250	| `ExternalDone` | External use of storage has ended when `unpin` is permitted |
251	| `Deallocable` | The place belongs to a unit that can actually be freed |
252	| `FreeCompat` | Opaque deallocation authority is compatible with the unit being freed |
253	| `Satisfiable` | The provider can satisfy the requested shape **in the current state** |
254	
255	Structural conditions of `free`, dependencies, and the derived library `reset` carry the relevant invalidation obligations. Physical justification of `DDSound` must be established by a realization consistent with memory layouts and Section 82.
256	
257	## 81. Boundaries Remaining to Be Specified
258	
259	This specification **does not by itself determine**: concurrency and synchronization effects (Spec 2); control-flow analysis, `defer`, and by-value calling conventions (Spec 3); representation criteria and typed formation of accesses (Spec 4); representation of library metadata, address width, encodings, and alignment/ABI obligations (Spec 11); or final translation of `noalias` properties (Spec 13). Leaving a rule open does not authorize a safe interface to cause UB; the implementation must fulfill or reject the obligations before exposing the operation to safe code.
260	
261	# XVII. Correspondence Between Access Discipline and Memory Machine
262	
263	A transition of the access discipline must admit a realization compatible with the bytes and allocations of the memory machine. An abstract definition of a right does not suffice to justify its concrete representation.
264	
265	## 82. Representation Relation and Concrete Obligations
266	
267	1. **Places and bytes:** relate `P`, `footprint` leaves, their ownership, and their parts to the storage units, offsets, ranges, identities, and alignment constraints of the elementary memory machine; establish actual disjointness for `DeclaredDisjoint` declarations.
268	2. **Authorities and operations:** connect effective modes and `ExercisableAt` to concrete read, write, and pointer-validity conditions; show that safe access governed by Parts VI through XV satisfies the obligations of Part III, without conflating ownership and binary representation. A pointer to a region whose leaves all have zero physical size is represented like a pointer to the empty region: its address is the base of the allocation of the effective anchor of its authority, and that allocation is its provenance.
269	3. **Initialization:** relate `Uninit`, `Init`, and `Moved` to concrete values and representations; an authority `store` must correspond to writing an actual reference into **a single logical leaf** with an appropriate representation.
270	4. **Allocation and deallocation:** relate `alloc` / `free` to `AllocStep` / `DeallocStep`, justify `Satisfiable`, `Deallocable`, and `FreeCompat`, as well as the zero-physical-size case.
271	5. **Lifetimes:** relate `endUse`, `exitFrame`, `NoDangling`, dependencies, and death markers to the validity effects on actual storage.
272	6. **Pinning and static storage:** prove compatibility of permitted moves and pinned-address restrictions; specify the physical obligations of statics and external use. Hardware-specific MMIO semantics remain outside the sequential kernel.
273	7. **Arenas:** show that the library abstraction's derived operations and metadata, distinct from `S₃`, can be realized by operations O1–O16; relate issued regions and local/static/allocated storage to the elementary memory machine without reintroducing access after invalidation.
274	8. **`noalias`:** infer no pointer-lowering property from abstract invariants alone; memory justification is established here and the translation choices at Spec 13 level.
275	
276	# XVIII. Examples of Semantic Behavior
277	
278	The fragments below are **traces of abstract operations**, not language syntax. The judgments illustrate normative rules; they create no exception to the detailed preconditions.
279	
280	## 83. Address Reuse and Old Provenance
281	
282	An allocation `a` is created and an access retains its provenance; after deallocation, a new allocation `b` may occupy the same address. `a ≠ b` as abstract identities: reading through the old access is invalid even if the addresses are equal. A new valid access with provenance `b` may be used within its rights.
283	
284	## 84. Partial Initialization and Reading
285	
286	A valid write to a subrange initializes its corresponding bytes. Reading another subrange that remains uninitialized is not permitted. The correspondence for logical state `Init` must guarantee a representation valid for the expected type; the mere presence of bits does not authorize type confusion.
287	
288	## 85. Splitting a Structure or SoA Columns
289	
290	Starting from a `Modify` authority exercised over a structure, `split` may provide `Modify` authorities over disjoint leaf regions. Modification of each region is permitted as long as the other validity and holder conditions hold; a second independent derivation over the same leaf does not become legal merely by having a distinct name.
291	
292	## 86. Arena, Active Views, and Reset
293	
294	Two disjoint issued regions may be used simultaneously with valid derived rights. `reset` is rejected while an issuance or active dependency would make recycling unsafe; after a legal end of use for all the relevant blocks, the region may be reissued. Reissuance modifies neither the bytes nor the initialization state. A read remains subject to the ordinary conditions of the memory model, notably `Init`, access rights, and representation validity for the requested type. Spec 4 will determine the construction and typing obligations of reissued values.
295	
296	## 87. Pinning an In-Place Value
297	
298	A pinned in-place leaf cannot be physically moved by `transfer`. If only an allocation owned by a value is pinned, transfer of that value may remain valid when the other conditions hold, because the owned allocation is not physically moved.
299	
300	## 88. Local Self-Blocking and Indirect Cycles
301	
302	An authority stored by `transfer` in a place that would then become its new holder cannot cover any leaf of that place. Likewise, `issue` cannot issue into a leaf belonging to the issued region, **or into a destination that would no longer be exercisable in `Modify` in the resulting state** (O8.5). These restrictions do not promise general freedom from authority cycles: indirect blocking compatible with safety may remain.
303	
304	## 89. Handles and Persistent References
305	
306	In a generation-based pool library abstraction, a handle may contain a logical pool identity, an entry identifier, and a generation. This handle is not, by itself, an access right. Safe resolution temporarily supplies authority when the pool and entry are valid; a stale identity or generation leads to defined failure. These conditions belong to the safe abstraction's contract and do not modify the authority-discipline kernel.
307	
308	## 90. Global and Called Frame
309	
310	Global storage is anchored to the base frame, but a called function does not acquire ambient authority to modify it merely by being invoked. To access a global, it receives a derived authority under `enterFrame` conditions and may exercise only its effective modes.
311

**Why:** the briefs require French commit messages (one per step), docstrings citing `MM-0x.y` rules, statement changes justified in the report, and say `formal/reports/` is exploration never merged into `main`. Later briefs add "arbitrages" that answer earlier report questions.

**How to apply:** start a new pass from the latest branch tip; run an adversarial review workflow over module and report before delivering; `lake` is not on PATH, call `~/.elan/bin/lake`; keep the Lake library name `Ern`. `formal/Ern/.gitkeep` keeps showing as deleted: restore it with `git checkout`, never commit the deletion. A post-commit hook can make `git commit` exceed 2 minutes: give it a long timeout. The axiom rule ({propext, Quot.sound} only) forbids core lemmas that pull `Classical.choice` (`List.getElem?_mapIdx`, `List.eq_nil_iff_forall_not_mem`, `List.nodup_range`, `List.pairwise_lt_range`): sweep `#print axioms` over every theorem and replace them with local lemmas. Mathlib tactics (`set`, `tauto`) are unavailable. Reviews keep catching report errors: quote old forms from the old commit, count declarations with a command, and base an evidence claim only on a check that would fail on the defect. After fixing review findings, run a second targeted review of the fixes: in MM-03 pass 2 a fix over-rejected legitimate programs. Before calling a clause "missing" from an arbitrage, re-read every earlier arbitrage still in force: in pass 3 the clause needed for exitFrame_no_dangling was A4's root-holder rule, which A1 puts in WF3 and pass 2 had left out. `timeout` does not exist on this Mac: run `lake build` directly (about 2.5 min). When an arbitrage enlarges a definition used in hypotheses (pass 4: `Inv3` gained `NoDangling`), theorems whose text is unchanged silently narrow: give them only the conjunct they use. Before retiring a counterexample whose witness breaks a new invariant clause, look for another witness: pass-4 review found one and flagged the weakening as major. Check obligations against the initial state: the base frame of `S3.init` owns no place, so an obligation about it can be vacuous on reached states. A review fix can itself pick a semantic reading (pass 5: the kind conjunct of `IsInternalFor` rejected a `newArena` that D3 leaves undecided): check every fix for verdicts it changes on cases the text is silent on. Module docstrings must cite the report's own numbering, not the review's decision numbers. Arbiter-supplied theorems can be false: check them on small reached states (owned storage, a parameter that is the ancestor of another) before trying a proof. Every factual claim in the report needs a module witness, or reviewers flag it; never say "blocked until X" without checking escape sequences such as ending the owner value. When a precondition gains clauses, lemmas taking it as a hypothesis narrow silently: name the old precondition (pass 7: `EnterPreBase`) and give the lemmas only what they use. A guard on one operation (G2 on `store`) is usually bypassable through another (a helper authority then `release`/`endUse`/`free`/exit): look for such bypasses before claiming a configuration is excluded. A new check on an operation with a defined failure (`issue` → `fail`) must not turn that failure into `reject`. Use one adversarial reviewer per arbitrage lens; each found distinct real issues in pass 7. When a restriction rejects an old counterexample, try to rebuild a witness that satisfies the new clause before restating it as a rejection (pass 8: a same-shape destination restored `transfer_not_inv3_preserving`). Drop hypotheses a proof does not use. When cases disappear because their state is no longer reached, replay their verdicts on a new reachable state and list the drops. Machine-check every changed verdict the report lists, including the old witnesses' rejected steps. Never state "only clause X fails" as `X → Pre` next to `¬ X`: that is vacuous; name the other clauses (pass 8: `TransferPreBase` with an iff) and state them. Run a second targeted check after fixing verification findings: in pass 8 it caught that vacuous form. `omega` proving a conjunction goal pulls `Classical.choice`: split the goal first. `meta` is a keyword in this Lean: never name a hypothesis `meta`. `set` (Mathlib) is unavailable: use `obtain ⟨x, hx⟩ : ∃ x, x = e := ⟨_, rfl⟩`. `if_pos`/`if_neg`/`ite_cond_eq_true` are deprecated: use `simp only [h, ↓reduceIte]`. When `S3.Usable.mono` is applied with `rfl` for `hP`, give `(s := …) (s' := …)` explicitly or it unifies the wrong way. Simulation theorems: never quantify obligations over all translations (vacuous); put them as per-step premises of the run with parameters fixed once, and give a concrete multi-step run as witness. A universal encoding obligation (`∀ addr, decode (enc addr) = addr`) is unsatisfiable by a finite computable decode: state it per value. `lake env lean` uses the last built olean: rebuild the module before a scratch file uses new declarations. Never use an unquoted heredoc for Lean or docstrings: backticks run as shell commands; use `<<'EOF'` and pass paths by environment variable. `example`s escape a `collectAxioms` sweep: rename them to theorems in a scratch copy to check their axioms. `awk length` counts bytes, not characters: count line length in Python. Each check round finds errors in the previous round's wording: when a sentence is fixed in a docstring, grep the report for the same claim; quote arbitrages exactly (L2 said "hypothèse des énoncés", not "hors langage"); classify every item a deliverable asks to classify instead of moving it aside; a summary must not present a hypothesis restated in a conclusion as a result. Count theorem constants with internal ones (`isInternal`) and say which count you give. A callee cannot move a value out of a parameter's footprint (`ActiveDerivedOutside` counts the parameter itself): build values to transfer as callee locals. Authority ids shift with every alloc/issue/split: check them with `#eval` of `prun` prefixes before writing a case. A literal invariant from the material can fail under the full kernel extension: keep the literal statement with counterexamples and prove the parts that hold, under their own names. A runner's fallback state must be unreachable (e.g. no frame) or a statement "the run's state is reached" is vacuous when the run fails; give a lemma deriving success from reachability. Projecting `.2` out of an existential passes the elaborator but fails in the kernel: use `obtain`. When `step_ok_of`-style lemmas time out at `whnf`, pass the contract `k` and statics explicitly. Jalon 3 took four check rounds (11/9/9/4 confirmed): each round's fixes need their own narrow check. The list `Sublist` notation `<+` is scoped: write `List.Sublist`; `List.take_add` pulls `Classical.choice`. `omit … in` goes before the docstring. A `def` in a `variable (k : K)` section takes `k` only if it uses it: check call sites. In a multi-line `{ st with … }`, put each field on its own line at one column. Theorems stated for registered arenas (`ar ∈ s.arenas`) do not carry over to library instances: never cite them for one. Before writing "the only effect of X is Y", look for a witness in the other direction (derivability: the missing guard also turned a `fail` into an `ok`).
